articleTitle: Cross-Domain Machine Learning Approaches using Hyperspectral Imaging for Plastics litter detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Plastics detection and polymer separation are important tasks for environmental monitoring and waste recycling. The authors previously used hyperspectral data in the lower bands of the SWIR range from 900nm to 1700 nm to perform plastics classification, by applying supervised machine learning methods to data gathered by a custom-assembled stand-alone push-broom system in indoor and outdoor conditions. In this work, we explored the application of two unsupervised learning algorithms: K-Means clustering and Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM), in order to avoid the use of a manually-labeled test set, and to obtain more reliable and flexible application in different environmental conditions. The results suggest that GMM performs well indoors but poorly outside, with GMM exhibiting subtle segmentation and K-Means displaying broader, more generalist categorization. The cross-domain adaptation is difficult and models that balance granularity and generalization are needed to detect plastic in varied settings. This effort advances garbage management and recycling and establishes hyperspectral imaging in real-world environments.

articleTitle: Grace-Based Observations for Near Real-Time Assessment of Groundwater Drought Severity Index
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: We propose in the this contribution a satellite-based method for regional assessment of the Palmer-type index of groundwater drought severity (GDSI) at monthly time scale in the North-Western Sahara Aquifer System (NWSAS). The proposed method is based on groundwater storage anomalies derived from GRACE satellites (Gravity Recovery And Climate Experiment) and GRACE Follow On (GRACE-FO) observations, combined with global hydrological models. We have applied an efficient strategy to estimate a (1°x1°) grid-cells time-series of GGDI (GRACE Groundwater Drought Index) from these anomalies, based upon a statistical analysis and procedures to filter out the anthropogenic trends. In second step of our methodology, an approach based on wavelet coherence was applied to the GGDI grid-cells to perform the climate teleconnections analysis, to detect an eventual relationship with climatic factors inducing extreme climate events. By comparing the obtained GGDI along NWSAS regions to other hydrological drought indices as PDSI (Palmer Drought Severity Index) and SPEI (Standardized Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index), we have allowed us to highlight the performance of the proposed method to monitor in near-real time the droughts/floods events occurred on the studied area. The obtained results have also revealed the existence of some correlation between the GGDI and ENSO time series and other climate indices not presented herein, reflecting some periods of drought/flood, occurred in different regions of NWSAS. These findings can be a novel information support to evaluate the natural effects on the groundwater recharge and depletion rates.

articleTitle: Cereal Crop Monitoring Using Sentinel Time Series Through Google Earth Engine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: In this study, we propose an approach based on Google Earth Engine (GEE) divided into two distinct steps. First, we use vegetation indices such as Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI), Leaf Area Index (LAI) and Harvest Index (HI). NDVI was used to characterize the growth stages of cereal crops and Otsu thresholding to extract cereal crops. The second step involved associating multitemporal datasets, containing a combination of spectral bands and vegetation indices, as input data for random forest (RF) machine learning classifiers to identify cereal crops. The classification accuracies reveal the show that the RF-NDVI provides an overall of 86.6% for cereal crop mapping, outperforming other techniques employed in this study, notably NDVI thresholding (70.7%), RF-EVI (80%), and RF-LAI (80%).

articleTitle: Hammam Melouane Sequence (2013-2016) for Faults Identification by Remote Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: During the 2013 to 2016 period, the Hammam Melouane region was the theatre of three recorded earthquakes, highlighting persistent seismic activity and suggesting the presence of asperities likely to trigger significant earthquakes. The purpose of this work is to map lineaments in order to isolate main fault of Hammam Melouane based on remote sensing images processing of the southern edge of the Mitidja basin. The obtained map shows areas of high structural density trended toward the N-S, NE-SW and NW-SE overlap and confirm the directions of all the events of the recorded seismic sequence, and as well as those of the focal mechanisms of the three main shocks recorded in the region from 2013 to 2016.

articleTitle: Insar-Based Stability Evaluation of a Motorway: The Oran-Tlemcen Segment of Algeria's East-West Highway as a Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Monitoring road infrastructure and its spatiotemporal dynamics is crucial for environmental, economic, and social well-being. Advanced methods, such as Persistent Scatterer Interferometry (PSI), allow vertical displacements to be detected at the sub-centimeter level. In this study, PSI is used to monitor the vertical displacements of the western section of the East-West Algerian highway, from Maghnia in Tlemcen to Oran. 60 Sentinel-1 radar images are used for this purpose. The radar interferometry is compared with the results of time series spectral analysis of the points identified on the highway. In addition, PSI interferometry makes it possible to detect potential degradation zones which can serve as a support for identifying the parts of the highway to be maintained.

articleTitle: Remote Sensing for Swelling Clay
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: This research focuses on the application of advanced remote sensing methods to detect and monitor swelling clay phenomena in the Mzila region, using data from various imaging sources. The initial phase involves utilizing the Spectral Angle Mapper technique on hyperspectral data from the Hyperion image to detect and identify clay minerals, particularly montmorillonite, in a specific bentonite mine.Subsequently, a time series of SAR images was processed using the SBAS technique to observe displacements over time. The obtained results visualized a series of dis-placements corresponding to the identified clay swelling phenomenon. To strengthen this conclusion, a comparative analysis was conducted by linking displacement data with precipitation and soil moisture data. This comparison confirmed that the observed displacements are directly related to variations in these environmental factors.This study demonstrates the effectiveness of the combined use of hyperspectral and radar remote sensing techniques for monitoring and understanding clay swelling phenomena, providing valuable insights for the management and prevention of risks associated with such terrain in the Mzila region.

articleTitle: Application of hybrid fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process AHP model for mapping alteration zones in Guelma basin; Eastern of Algeria
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The fusion and analysis of multiple criteria is a critical step in increasing the precision of the location of areas of mineral potential during the mineral discovery phase. The study aims to provide a potential map of the hydrothermal alteration zones responsible for the formation of antimony mineralisation in the Guelma region, based on criteria derived from geological and remote sensing data. Remote sensing and GIS techniques were jointly applied to prepare and integrate several factors contributing to the mineralisation occurrences. Remote sensing techniques such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Minimum Noise Fraction (MNF), Band Ratio (BR), False Color Composite (FCC) and were used to define the geological characteristics of the study area including lithological units, structural features and hydrothermal alteration zones. The thematic layers extracted from each criterion were evaluated using a hybrid fuzzy _AHP model. The results of the applications in this study provide an acceptable map defining the areas that may contain antimony mineralisation in the Guelma region.The results of the method were in good agreement with known mineralisation in the area and could be used as a means of exploring for future deposits.

articleTitle: Lithological Descrimination and Slope Gradient for the Adjusted Hydrologic Soil Group Mapping in the Hodna Watershed
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: This paper aims to develop a concept for the adjusting the Hydrologic Soil Group mapping using the lithological discrimination techniques and the slope gradient. This adjustment process will refine the delineation of hydrological groups by taking into account the slope gradient variation. This approach provides enhanced accuracy in classifying soils based on their hydrological behavior, considering topographical nuances that may impact soil infiltration capacity. By integrating these insights, the resulting hydrological mapping becomes more detailed and better suited to the specific conditions of the study area.

articleTitle: Flood Susceptibility Mapping Using Multi Sensor Time Series Data in Middle Brahmaputra Basin
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The state of Assam in India is ubiquitous of the periodic flood events that disrupts people’s social and economic lives every year. Understanding the dynamics of recurrent flood events is helpful for risk reduction and mitigation. An effort has been made in this study to comprehend the Brahmaputra flooding by dividing the frequently flooded area into four separate Flood Plains (FPs), and by studying each region using multitemporal, multi sensor data from years 2016-2022. Each FP is studied for flood susceptibility using Analytical Hierarchical Process (AHP). A single flood plain has been chosen and mapped based on the susceptibility, number of flood hits and maximum flood depth. For the selected flood plain, the flood conditioning factors are closely studied.

articleTitle: Prisma Images for the Estimation of Functional Traits and Biodiversity Indices in Mid-Latitude Forests
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: In this contribution, we exploit hyperspectral data cubes collected by the PRISMA satellite to develop and test machine learning regression algorithms (MLRAS) for mapping forest traits and estimating spatial patterns of plant beta diversity in mixed forest ecosystems. The MLRAs were trained using PRISMA data and ground data collected in correspondence of the satellite overpasses. Based on their ecological importance, leaf chlorophyll content, leaf water content, leaf mass area, leaf nitrogen content and leaf area index were investigated. Finally, emerging methods aimed at the estimation of forest biodiversity based on spectral diversity were applied to hyperspectral images.Results showed that MLRAs performed well in leaf and canopy traits retrieval with high predictive capacity for all the models tested. Moreover, the spatio-temporal patterns of functional traits generally agreed with the spectral diversity patterns.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal Influence of Lulc Change and Their Effect on the Hydrological Response of a Semi-Arid Watershed
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The alteration in land use and land cover, primarily linked to anthropogenic activities, especially in arid and semi-arid areas, which are highly sensitive to changes, directly influences the evolution of the hydrological response of watersheds. This paper aims to manage the hydrological response of the wadi saida watershed according the spatiotemporal change of the LULC using SCS-DUH and analyzing variation of the peak flow at different lag time, in creating the runoff hydrograph.

articleTitle: Assessing Current and Future Land Subsidence Risk Induced by Groundwater Exploitation in Italy Using Earth Observation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Earth observation data and advanced modeling are used in this work to generate products and tools aiming to enhance the understanding of subsidence risk in major urban areas of Italy, towards sustainable use of groundwater resources and urban development. A multi-scale methodology is designed to assess present-day subsidence risk using satellite-based ground deformation observations, hydrogeological, topographic and land use data, and to identify subsidence hotspots and drivers using geostatistics. Advanced numerical modelling coupling 3D transient groundwater flow and geomechanics enables quantification of the effects of groundwater usage to land deformation. Future subsidence risk under climate change scenarios, demographic and urban development, is assessed by adapting the advanced model. Market and non-market direct/indirect losses are quantified via a bespoke socio-economic impact analysis.

articleTitle: A Taxonomy of Relationships Between Information Processing, Machine Learning and Quantum Physics: Quantum-Inspired, Quantum-Assisted, Quantum-Targeted and Related Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: In this paper, we provide an overview of the connections that were developed, during the current second quantum revolution, between information processing (IP) and machine learning (ML) in the classical (i.e. non-quantum) framework on the one hand, and several aspects of quantum physics on the other hand, namely properties involved in quantum theory and practical implementations leading to quantum computers. Moreover, we propose a taxonomy of the new fields resulting from these connections, both at the general level of IP methods and at the more specific level of data-driven, i.e. ML, methods. We thus consider quantum-inspired (or quantum-like), quantum-assisted (or quantum-enhanced), quantum-executed and quantum-targeted IP and ML methods.

articleTitle: Application of deep neural networks to groundwater potential mapping in the region of Sidi Bel Abbès, Algeria
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Groundwater potential mapping becomes key to several fields due to water shortages and drought impacts. During this work, we apply deep neural networks to delineate the potential zones in the plain of Sidi Bel Abbès. The methods aim at producing a reliable estimation of the potential zones based on the groundwater static level. The model is constructed as a compromise between simplicity as well as efficiency. As model features, we employ seven thematic maps which are: digital elevation model, slope, drainage, lineaments, land use, rainfall and lithology. Results show that the proposed method achieves better performance compared to several machine learning methods (RF, SVM and Neural Networks) in terms of accuracy (84.94%) and κ (0.80) coefficient with excellent AUC (0.80). The predicted maps can be used to improve the management of groundwater resources in the region.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Change Detection System Using ORB and Principal Component Analysis for Application on-Board Earth Observation Satellites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Change detection systems on-board satellites aim to decrease the amount of data transmitted to the ground station by sending only the part of the image containing the identified changes, referred to as change image. The objective of this paper is to propose an automatic change detection system for application on-board earth observation satellites. The aim is to provide useful information of the changes in disaster affected areas and to issue early warnings. The proposed system is based on two modules: a registration module based on Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF (ORB) algorithm and a change detection module based on Principal Components Analysis (PCA). The performance of the proposed system is evaluated using real satellite images of the Algerian Satellites Alsat-1b and Alsat-2. The results are scaled and compared to existing hardware used on-board Algerian Earth observation satellites.

articleTitle: The Potentials of Large-Scale Open Access Remotely Sensed Ready Products: Use and Recommendations when Monitoring Urban Sprawl Near Cultural Heritage Sites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Recent studies show how remote sensing data elaboration practices have been shifted from (pre and post) processing of a few number of satellite images, to the use of an extensive dataset. Ready calibrated and validated satellite products, have been populated lately in the literature, driven by the open access policy of space agencies such as those of the European Space Agency (ESA), advance image processing (e.g., deep learning and machine learning) and availability of big data cloud infrastructures.Nevertheless, this shift has not yet well-fitted with research questions and needs of a range of disciplines considered to be "application fields" from a geomatic and geospatial science perspective. In this paper we aim to showcase the challenges when using sophisticated collections such as Global Human Settlement Layer (GHSL) data for heritage applications. Cultural heritage domain relies on remote sensing information for purposes of mapping, monitoring and management and often requires tailored made considerations on the changing context that surrounds the single sites is presented. The paper gives some indications on use and recommendations when using this kind of data for monitoring urban sprawl near some cultural heritage sites in Cyprus.

articleTitle: Comparative study of pansharpening remote sensing techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Pansharpening involves merging multispectral (MS) imagery and panchromatic (PAN) data to generate an output that matches the spatial resolution of the PAN data and retains the spectral resolution of the MS image. Over the past three decades, numerous approaches have emerged to address this challenge. This study aims to provide a comprehensive assessment by benchmarking various MS pansharpening techniques. Specifically, it compares optimized classical methods such as multiresolution analysis (MRA) and component substitution (CS) with third-generation pansharpening methods like variational optimization (VO) and machine learning (ML) techniques. The evaluation is conducted using urban IKONOS (IK) images. Both reduced and full-resolution quantitative assessments are performed.

articleTitle: Convolutional Encoder-Decoder Network for Road Extraction from Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a convolutional neural network, which is based on down sampling followed by up sampling architecture for the purpose of road extraction from aerial images. Our model consists of convolutional layers only. The proposed encoder-decoder structure allows our network to retain boundary information, which is a critical feature for road identification. This feature is usually lost when dealing with other CNN models. Our design is also less complex in terms of depth, number of parameters, and memory size. It, therefore, uses fewer computer resources in both training and during execution. Experimental results on Massachusetts roads dataset demonstrate that the proposed architecture, although less complex, competes with the state-of-the-art proposed approaches in terms of precision, recall, and accuracy.

articleTitle: An Empirical Approach to Map the Paddy Crops at the Ripening Stage Using SLC and GRD Sentinel-1 Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Mapping the pre-harvest phenology of paddy crops in the coastal delta region is essential to investigate cyclonic storms’ impact on the anticipated crop yield for making informed agro-economic decisions. The present study was conducted for Agastheeswaram block, Kanniyakumari District, Tamil Nadu, which is being affected by frequent cyclonic storms that bring catastrophic damage to the paddy crops. The GRD (Ground Range Detected) and SLC (Side looking Complex) products of a Sentinel-1 C-band data in dual-polarization (VV+VH) were instrumental in this study. The SAR-based new empirical simulation PS3 (Paddy Stage 3) was proposed as a function of DPSVI (Dual Polarization SAR Vegetation Index) and Entropy measures retrieved from SLC and GRD products. The accuracy assessment with ground observations has demonstrated that the PS3 has higher potential (Overall Accuracy = 86.36%, Kappa Coefficient = 0.73, Precision = 0.88, Recall = 0.84) to delineate the paddy crops at their ripening phase.

articleTitle: Generalized Linear Mixing Model Based Environmental Monitoring Of Marine Mucilage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The marine mucilage outbreak of Spring 2021 in the inland Sea of Marmara raised significant environmental, economic and public-health related concerns. Recently, unmixing based approaches have been shown to provide spectral and spatial analysis of marine mucilage, in terms of endmembers and abundances. However, as the spectral signature of mucilage is prone to vary depending on factors such as its composition and density, and the characteristics of water in an inland sea are also highly dynamic, the linear mixture model (LMM) may be insufficient to correctly characterize the resulting mixture. This study proposes a Generalized Linear Mixing Model (GLMM) based unmixing approach to take spectral variability into account in unmixing based marine mucilage analysis. The proposed approach is evaluated on real PRISMA and DESIS hyperspectral data, and compared with LMM and Extended Linear Mixing Model (ELMM) based approaches.

articleTitle: Validation Of Global Forest Canopy Height Data In A Semi-Arid Algerian Forest Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The objective of this study was to assess the relevance of canopy height data for global forests in the context of a natural forest located in a semi-arid ecosystem of the Saharan Atlas. In the operational context of integrating this data into future national forest inventories, we calculated the root mean square errors (RMSE) using observed data for the years 2009 and 2023 with 151 and 78 plots, respectively. Validation results revealed RMSE values of 6.60 and 5.26 for the years 2009 and 2023, highlighting some uncertainty primarily attributed to saturation in forested areas and shadow effects. Precision also varies based on the structural parameters of forest stands.

articleTitle: Satellite Hands-On Learning Through ESAT Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The development of space technology opens the doors for gathering information related to the Earth’s atmosphere, lithosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere and human-induced changes, which was not possible in the past. Remote Sensing, Geoscience, Geographical Information System, and the Internet have made the collection, storage and dissemination of information easier than ever.

articleTitle: An ADMM-Based Approach Associated with a Linear Mixing Model Multiplicatively Tuned to Deal with Spectral Variability in Hyperspectral Unmixing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: In this work, a hyperspectral unmixing approach, based on an Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM), is proposed. This approach is designed for a linear mixing model in which the spectral variability phenomenon is spectrally modeled in a multiplicative manner. The study evaluates the performance of the designed ADMM-based algorithm against the gradient-descent-based algorithms previously proposed. Experiments, using synthetic hyperspectral data, are carried out and the obtained results show that the overall performance of the proposed approach is satisfactory and the proposed algorithm, globally, outperforms the tested approaches from the literature.

articleTitle: Detecting Desertification in Southern Morocco Using a Multi-Sensor, Random Forest Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Existing landcover products depicting degraded land do not accurately show the extent of desertification of traditional cultivation systems. These products rely on recent NDVI (Normalised Difference Vegetation Index) time series and statistical data. Historical desertification is missed, although these abandoned fields are distinctive in satellite imagery as reflectant and smooth surfaces. We present our Google Earth Engine workflow for detecting desertification using satellite data (full details are in our recent paper). We used the random forest algorithm to classify five landcover categories including desertified fields, applied to a data stack comprising a 13-band Sentinel-2 composite and derived tasselled cap components, and a Sentinel-1 VV-polarisation composite. We test our approach for case studies of the Skoura and Draa oases in southern Morocco with a resulting accuracy of 74-76% for the desertification class.

articleTitle: Temporal Analysis of Land Surface Temperatures Dynamics In Damascus, Syria, Using Google Earth Engine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: This study uses remote sensing and geographic information systems (GIS) to investigate the urban heat island (UHI) phenomenon in Damascus, Syria, over ten years (2013-2022). The study uses Google Earth Engine, Landsat 8, and MODIS data to investigate surface temperature dynamics and their relationship to the Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and Normalised Difference Built-up Index (NDBI). The results show a significant increase in urbanized areas at the expense of green spaces. Observe an increase in urbanized areas from 2013 (0.2) to 2022 (0.27). Land Surface Temperature (LST) analysis reveals higher temperatures in 2022 compared to 2013. A temperature increase of 1.6 °C is observed, indicating the presence of a UHI during the day. Spatial variations in the heat island are consistent with industrial concentrations. Linear regression analyses show a negative correlation between NDVI and LST, indicating that vegetative cover decreases as temperatures rise. In contrast, a strong positive correlation is observed between NDBI and temperature, highlighting the impact of built-up areas on elevated temperatures.

articleTitle: Exploring CNN for urban area Extraction from Polarimetric SAR data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The convolutional neural networks CNNs have been widely used in pattern recognition and image processing in the last ten years. This paper intends to identify the urban area from polarimetric Synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) data using the CNN model. This model has shown its effectiveness in classification. For this purpose, we propose to use a feature vector that contains the elements of the circular matrix and the calculated parameters from Cloude decomposition (entropy, alpha angle and anisotropy). The used elements are roll invariants, which make them not sensitive to the orientation angle, which can create ambiguity between oriented buildings and vegetation. To test the performance of the proposed method, ALOS-2/PALSAR-2L-band and AIRSAR C-band over the San-Francisco, USA were used. The results show that man-made targets could be effectively discriminated from natural scenes using the proposed method.

articleTitle: Exploring Synthetic Captions for Remote Sensing Vision-Text Foundational Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Large multi-modal models, empowered with both textual and visual inputs, have shown tremendous capabilities in a wide range of vision and language tasks. This kind of vision-text models, extensively studied in natural settings, are receiving less attention in the remote sensing (RS) field. Oftentimes, RS research relies on models for natural scenarios, glossing over the potential improvements of systems tailored to the remote sensing scenario. In this paper, we push toward bridging this gap. First, we design a procedure to generate a large-scale RS image-text dataset with synthetic captions. We use it to fine-tune a targeted CLIP model and we analyze the effect of using only synthetic captions on the model capabilities. Lastly, we build a benchmark for remote sensing image-text models, and evaluate our model, along with other recently proposed in the literature. We release the code of our benchmark system and our dataset.

articleTitle: Shadow Buildings analysis for seismic damage assesment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: After a natural disaster occurrence, such as earthquakes, the remote sensing often remains a substantial way to detect the extent of disaster. It allows the implementation of a real time post-disaster management plans, mobilization of emergency, coordination of seeking, rescue and mapping the damage spatial distribution.With the advent of the very high resolution satellites, the opportunities to improve the frequency and quality of urban data have emerged. The very high resolution satellites, whose discrimination power of objects on the ground can help to quickly develop useful tools to various stakeholders in post disaster crisis.This paper aims to develop an automatic process for detecting buildings height, throughits shadow form Quick Bird images analysis. The extraction of the building shadow is performed through a panchromatic channel, the size of the shadow and the height of the building are then extracted from a developed program under Matlab software. This method has the main advantage of being independent of time and season and the skill of the photo interpreter.The method is used for the detection of post-earthquake construction damages that occurred after Boumerdes earthquake of May 21<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> 2003. Six buildings are considered and the results show a good agreement with the in situ observations.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Machine Learning Algorithms for Glacier facies Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Classification of different glacier facies are the important factors which determine the rate of retreat/advance of a glacier. In this paper, the potential of using freely available Sentinel-1 radar images for glacier zones mapping in the Chandra basin of Himachal Pradesh is examined. The three images of three different months (January, May & September) used and different supervised algorithms namely MD, MLC and SVM were implemented. Google earth imagery and RGB stacked image was used to create training dataset which is used to train the model. Post processing of the classification results overall accuracy have been calculated. It is found that the significantly better accuracy was achieved through support vector machines i.e. more than 90%.

articleTitle: Exploring the Mila Landslide: Integrating Radar and Optical Remote Sensing for Enhanced Geohazard Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: This conference paper presents a comprehensive remote sensing study aimed at investigating the Mila landslide triggered by a moderate earthquake on August 7, 2020. Leveraging Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 radar and optical imagery, Coherence Change Detection and Change Detection techniques were applied to delineate the landslide area. Discrepancies between radar and optical-derived results highlighted the strengths and limitations of each modality in accurately delineating the affected area.Additionally, displacement estimation was performed using Sentinel-1 radar data through Offset Tracking and compared to estimations derived from Sentinel-2 and AlSat-2A optical imagery processed with MPIC-OPT and Cosi-Corr software. Surpassing accuracy observed in optical imagery-based displacement estimations emphasized the finer spatial resolution’s significance in capturing detailed surface alterations.Further analyses involving ALOS DSM data revealed lineaments coinciding with landslide boundaries, suggesting potential subsurface fault structures manifesting as surface lineaments. These findings contribute to understanding lithological influences in landslide predisposition.Collectively, the integration of diverse remote sensing techniques offers multifaceted insights into the Mila landslide, emphasizing the importance of combining radar and optical data for comprehensive assessments. The outcomes underscore remote sensing's pivotal role in unraveling complex geohazards, thereby enhancing our understanding and management strategies in landslide-prone areas.

articleTitle: Geospatial and Hydrochemical Analysis of Surface Water and Groundwater Quality of Inland Water Bodies for The Region of India Using Interpolation Techniques and Kriging Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The water quality in the Indian subcontinent’s surface water and groundwater is deteriorating rapidly. According to the CWMI by NITI Aayog, 70% of India’s water supply is contaminated nationally. Previous studies have focused on evaluating water quality changes at a sub-regional scale within watershed basins and rivers spanning significant cities. This study delves into spatial and temporal data analysis for the Indian River water basin from 2011 to 2019. Surface water samples were collected by regional remote sensing centres, with data managed by the State Pollution Control Board as part of India-Water Resource Information Services under the Ministry of Jal Shakti. A structured data repository was created for laboratory data parameters, including carbonate, bicarbonate, pH, turbidity, electrical conductivity, and other parameters. The analysis focused on Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, utilizing interpolation techniques like Kriging and IDW. Such techniques help in minimizing bias in prediction. The Kriging predictor is an "optimal linear predictor", ensuring that every interpolated value is computed to minimize the prediction error at that specific point. A 95% confidence interval was established for Hydrogen carbonate concentration and a 90-92% confidence interval for sodium (Na) and Potassium (K). The validation process showed an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (coefficient of determination) value of 84% for hydrogen carbonate and 82% for sodium and potassium, indicating a robust analysis methodology.

articleTitle: NVDI- and NBR-based Comparison for Burnt Areas Characterization Using Sentinel-2 Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Mapping the risk of areas susceptible to forest fires requires the use of new techniques such as remote sensing and geographic information systems (GIS), which are complementary tools to the conventional methods used to undertake prevention and response management actions. Accurate and rapid mapping of fire-affected areas is fundamental to support fire management, take account of environmental losses, define planning strategies and monitor vegetation restoration. Remote sensing is used for forest fire detection, monitoring and post-fire vegetation regrowth. Remote sensing data can be used to locate active fires and subsequent hotspots. Comparison between burnt areas and active fires provides information on fire speed and direction. The integration of satellite imagery in the fight against forest fires will make it possible to identify areas affected by forest fires, particularly those that are inaccessible, and to improve forest fire assessments by providing a more refined and accurate delimitation, and by taking into account burnt areas in inaccessible zones that Forest managers were unable to estimate. Annual monitoring of forest fires using satellite imagery gives a global view and provides very useful information on the environment, for a wide range of scales, and establishes a status of forest areas covered by fire, mainly during heatwave periods. To characterize burnt areas, we can use the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) or Normalized Burn Ratio (NBR). This study tries to measure the difference between these two methodologies. In results, the NBR index gives results that are more precise, it only indicates burnt surfaces areas, whereas the NDVI can include bare land surfaces for example.

articleTitle: Enhancing Road Network Extraction from Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Satellite image analysis for road network information extraction is crucial, particularly in remote sensing. This initiative is significant for urban planning, real-time road map updates, and autonomous driving technology development. However, challenges arise, including small-scale roads, complex paths, and potential obscuration in satellite images, complicating detection by deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNNs). This article evaluates three road network extraction models U-Net, LinkNet34, and LinkNet34++—emphasizing data augmentation benefits. LinkNet34, based on ResNet34, stands out for efficiency, using a pretrained network for accelerated learning, especially suitable for medium-resolution images. Our study assesses accuracy, recall, F1 score, and Jaccard Index (IoU) comprehensively with a diverse dataset. Metrics highlight LinkNet34++'s superior efficiency compared to U-Net and LinkNet34, particularly with applied data augmentation, showcasing its capability to handle road image variability and enhance overall model robustness in road network extraction.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Characteristics of Sea-Level Anomalies in the Mediterranean Coast
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: In this study, we analyze the variations in sea level observed at Tide Gauge stations across the Mediterranean Sea, utilizing datasets spanning over 50 years. Our investigation focuses on identifying various cycles, seasonal patterns, and non-seasonal fluctuations within the data collected from the selected tide gauge stations. We employ empirical mode decomposition (EMD) and the Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT) to examine these patterns comprehensively. Additionally, we investigate the relationship between Sea Level Anomalies (SLA) and major climate phenomena such as the North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO), Atlantic Multidecadal Oscillation (AMO) and El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO). Our findings reveal a significant connection between the SLA and the NAO at higher frequencies (less than 3 years), while the AMO appears to be more closely associated with a longer periodicity ( more than 15 years). In addition, the considerable fluctuations observed in the HHT analysis are found to be associated with ENSO events.

articleTitle: Quantum-Assisted Machine Learning by Means of Adiabatic Quantum Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Motivated by the potential performance gains offered by quantum computing (QC), a recent research focus — known as quantum-assisted machine learning (QAML) — aims to develop machine learning algorithms tailored for execution on quantum computers while processing data that originate from a classical (i.e. non-quantum) phenomenon. QAML has been studied in various quantum computing (QC) paradigms. This paper, in particular, offers a brief overview of QAML within the context of adiabatic quantum computing (AQC). The major challenge in this case is to reformulate the machine learning task as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem, which lies at the core of existing AQC physical implementations. We provide examples of machine learning techniques tailored to AQC, along with applications in remote sensing.

articleTitle: Applications Of Machine Learning Techniques In Predicting Selected Soil Properties In Lower Mississippi Alluvial Valley Green Tree Reservoir
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Measurement of fine-scale soil properties is important for understanding and monitoring the spatial distribution of soil properties, especially in wetland areas where soil classification data are often limited. This study applied three machine learning algorithms, i.e., random forest, decision tree, and support vector machine, to predict the spatial distribution of selected soil properties (Cation Exchange Capacity, Carbon, and Nitrogen) across 12 forested wetland stands also known as green tree reservoir (GTR), encompassing 1,200 acres in the Lower Mississippi Alluvial Valley of Arkansas. A total of 540 soil samples were collected across the GTRs at a depth of 0-15cm, 15-30cm, 30-50cm. The result from this study shows that the random forest algorithms performed best in predicting CEC, carbon and nitrogen at 0-15 cm and 15-30 cm depths with decision tree providing a higher prediction accuracy for carbon at the depth of 30-50 cm. Topographic derivatives such as elevation, generalized surface TOBIA index diurnal anisotropic heating and land surface temperature were the important predictors.

articleTitle: Land Surface Temperature Spatiotemporal Analysis In Relation To Earthquake Occurrence, Case Of Arzew In Algeria
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Studies of events associated to earthquakes are essential to fully understand and mitigate this type of natural disaster. In this work, survey of earthquake events is conducted by looking at deviations in Land Surface Temperatures (LST). The investigation is carried out by finding the relationship between changes in LST in relation to the earthquake that occurred on the 26 June 2022 (Mw = 4,5) at Arzew, in North-West of Algeria. Landsat-8 satellite imagery are used to get the values of LSTs using a Split-Window algorithm, which uses the two thermal bands of Landsat data, and the deviation that occurred is deduced from a statistical test, by comparing the average LST for June month of five years period. The results of the study is an increase in LST due to the earthquake occurrence. The increase is about 13,48°C on the day after the earthquake.

articleTitle: Sharpened VIIRS-NTL Data Using Modis Images for Improving Flared Gas Volume Estimations: Case of an Oil Installation in the South of Algeria
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: In this paper, sharpened multispectral VIIRS-NTL data are considered for the flared gas volume estimations task. Such data, with their finer spatial resolution obtained by using MODIS images, are intended to provide better localization of flare flames. Thus, these sharpened data are expected to provide improved estimations of flared gas volumes via some estimated physical flare parameters by means of a spectral-unmixing-based approach. Experiments are carried out on an oil installation located in the South of Algeria. Estimated flare gas volumes are compared with in-situ measurements, and these estimates are better than those obtained by using non-sharpened VIIRS-NTL data.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Potential of Surface Soil Moisture to Identify the Drought Periods in a Mediterranean Region (Tunisia)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The surface soil moisture is a main indicator of droughts. Therefore, in the present work, we analyzed the potential of two operational products of surface soil moisture, namely High-Resolution Soil Moisture (HRSM) and Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) to identify the drought periods. These climatic analyses are based on the examination of a drought index calculated as function of the monthly averages of soil moisture from 2017 to June 2022 according to the bioclimatic stages of the Tunisian territory. The proposed index’s time series are highlighted by minimum values of soil moisture since the end of the year 2021. This period is in coherence with the extreme drought period since 2021 in Tunisia.

articleTitle: Damage Assessment of Cyclone on the Mangrove Forest Using Remote Sensing Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Mangroves are considered as the unique ecosystems that thrive in the inter-tidal zones of tropical and subtropical coastlines. Beyond their ecological significance, mangroves are invaluable to communities as they offer protection against coastal erosion, sustain fisheries, and serve as a sustainable source of livelihood for many coastal populations. The present study aimed to investigate the impact of cyclone "Bulbul" on the mangrove ecosystem in the Sundarbans, India. In the present study, the NDVI simulation was employed for the Landsat8 data acquired for pre- and post-cyclone periods to investigate the dynamics in the forest cover. The ISODATA algorithm was performed for the Landsat8 data to classify the land cover classes. The performance of the classifier was validated with the ground truth observation supported by Google Earth (Overall accuracy=94%, Kappa coefficient =0.771813). The statistical analysis on the NDVIs retrieved for the mangrove category from ISODATA classifier shown that the biomass content of the forest has significantly reduced after the impact of the cyclone (NDVI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>(Pre-cyclone)=0.47, NDVI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>(Post-cyclone)=0.40). Hence, this study provides a broad insight into the damage assessment of the mangroves population

articleTitle: Nationwide Monitoring of Surface Motion Dynamics in Greece Exploiting Sentinel-1 Archive and EO Platform Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: We are presenting SAR interferometric processing efforts aimed at mapping surface motion across the entire Greek territory, including the totality of the islands. We introduce a nationwide surface motion product derived utilizing Copernicus Sentinel-1 mission and the on-demand SNAPPING service on the GEP platform. The totality of Copernicus Sentinel-1 archive over Greece in descending orbits was exploited covering the period between 04/2015 and 12/2021. As an outcome of the activity, a total number of 4M point measurements were detected, showing surface motion at medium resolution. Being generic, SNAPPING results enabled the quantification of motion and its dynamics for a rather broad spectrum of phenomena, comprising land subsidence, landslides, earthquake, tectonic movements and volcano deformation. Tiled products are publicly available on the GEP platform for both inspection and download by registered GEP users.

articleTitle: Automated Road Extraction with Rapid Visibility During Eartquakes using LiDAR Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The design of road routes, especially in urban areas, is crucial for effective transportation. Generally, image data and other geographic or satellite-based data sources are required for active extraction. However, in an emergency, such as an earthquake, this may not be adequate, therefore faster and more effective solutions may be required. This is achieved using automatic extraction using the Qgis plugin, Mapflow plugin and Rule Based Feature Extraction (RBFE) method using Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) point cloud data.The study found that the RBFE approach has an accuracy of 89%, while Mapflow has an accuracy of 92%. To improve the results, the Portion of Visible Sky (PCV) method and LiDAR-Digital Surface Model (DSM) image were used. At the end of the process, potential obstacles, such as trees or cars on the road, can be identified, which humans may not be able to detect remotely. In the future, the proposed methods could be further developed with the help of the OpenStreetMap data set.

articleTitle: Detecting Offsets in Annual Precipitations Time Series Case: East of Algeria
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Observations exploited in Meteorology and climatology as precipitations are affected by heterogeneities that are due to the change of equipment (GNSS antenna, rain gauge), treatment methodology, failure related to satellites, climatic natural effect ... etc.The main objective of this study is to apply some statistical methods that make it possible to detect breaks within the series of observations (Pettitt and SNHT test (Standard Normal Homogeneity test) ...). and adjust the time series. The time series of precipitation collected through this study were processed by different statistical methods and the obtained results are satisfying in the context of correlation between different methods, nevertheless, it would be desirable to use other longer datasets with more robust methods

articleTitle: An Informed ADMM-Based Approach for Hyperspectral Unmixing Addressing Additively-Adapted Spectral Variability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: In remote sensing, hyperspectral unmixing aims to identify the pure spectral signatures, known as "endmembers", present within each pixel of a hyperspectral image and to estimate the abundance fractions of each endmember. Hyperspectral unmixing accuracy is significantly affected by the spectral variability phenomenon. In this paper, a new informed hyperspectral unmixing approach, which deals with additively-adapted spectral variability, is introduced. This approach, in addition to taking into account the spectral variability phenomenon, exploits one or more known pure material spectra present in considered hyperspectral data. Based on the alternating direction multiplier method, the proposed method decomposes the observed mixed pixel spectra into constituent spectral signatures and corresponding abundance fractions. Simulation results, using semi-real data, demonstrate the robustness of the proposed method for unmixing hyperspectral data with spectral variability.

articleTitle: A Spectral Analysis-Based Approach for Methane Emission Estimations Using Landsat and Sentinel-2 Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Methane is the second most important greenhouse gas released into the atmosphere after carbon dioxide. Oil and gas industries represent one of the main sources of anthropological methane emissions. This is particularly noticeable in sporadic releases during maintenance operations or equipment failures. In this work, a spectral analysis-based approach is used for detecting and quantifying methane emissions utilizing two types of multispectral remote sensing data, namely Landsat and Sentinel-2 images. The investigation was carried out on an oil and gas installation located in the South of Algeria. These experiments reveal close similarities and a good agreement between the obtained results, in terms of detection and quantification of methane emissions, using Landsat data and those achieved through Sentinel-2 images. This constitutes a good indicator of the used spectral analysis-based approach reliability.

articleTitle: Randomized Principal Component Analysis for Hyperspectral Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The high-dimensional feature space of the hyperspectral imagery poses major challenges to the processing and analysis of the hyperspectral data sets. In such a case, dimensionality reduction is necessary to decrease the computational complexity. The random projections open up new ways of dimensionality reduction, especially for large data sets. In this paper, the principal component analysis (PCA) and randomized principal component analysis (R-PCA) for the classification of hyperspectral images using support vector machines (SVM) and light gradient boosting machines (LightGBM) have been investigated. In this experimental research, the number of features was reduced to 20 and 30 for classification of two hyperspectral datasets (Indian Pines and Pavia University). The experimental results demonstrated that PCA outperformed R-PCA for SVM for both datasets, but received close accuracy values for LightGBM. The highest classification accuracies were obtained as 0.9925 and 0.9639 by LightGBM with original features for the Pavia University and Indian Pines, respectively.

articleTitle: An Admm-Based Hyperspectral Unmixing Algorithm For A Modified Almm Addressing Spectral Variability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: This work presents a linear mixing model, and a related algorithm, for addressing spectral variability in hyperspectral unmixing. The research focuses on a variant of the modified Augmented Linear Mixing Model (mALMM), and the development and evaluation of an unmixing algorithm based on the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) concept. The new variant of the mALMM is introduced to model spectral variability, while the ADMM provides an optimization framework for unmixing hyperspectral data. The study evaluates the performance of the designed ADMM-based algorithm in comparison to a literature technique based on nonnegative matrix factorization. The experiments are conducted using synthetic hyperspectral data to assess the algorithm's effectiveness in handling spectral variability. The results demonstrate the attractiveness of the designed unmixing algorithm for hyperspectral data with spectral variability.

articleTitle: Comparing Chlorophyll Content Reflectance in Irrigated Parcels: A Study Using the Random Forest Algorithm and Chlorophyll Content Indexes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Chlorophyll content in vegetation is a key variable for assessing the physiological condition and photosynthetic activity of plants. This study aim to examine the relationship between reflectance and chlorophyll content in irrigated parcels (IPs) in the Mostaganem plateau aquifer land (Northwestern Algeria), using Chlorophyll Content Indices (ChICI) and a land cover classification approach. The latter approach uses unsupervised clustering to segment the pixel, followed by a Random Forest (RF) model to classify pixels into land cover types. The proposed methods are implemented in the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform, utilizing Sentinel-2 satellite imagery. The RF model was more effective at identifying and mapping IPs areas than approaches relying solely on chlorophyll-sensitive spectral bands and indexes derived from them. The confusion matrix analysis showed high-accuracy statistics. The overall accuracy was 0.91 and the Kappa coefficient was 0.83. For the IP class specifically, the sensitivity was 0.86.

articleTitle: Risk of Forest Fire; Evaluation and Detection Using Multicriteria Analysis and Spatial Data (Application to the Sidi Bel Abbes Forest Massif)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Forest fires are one of the primary environmental concerns, and Sidi Bel Abbes massif is particularly susceptible to recurring outbreaks. Between 2010 and 2022 there were 218 fires. The objective of this study was to assess the fire risk of the Sidi Bel Abbes forests before the summer season during two periods 2014-2020 using GIS tools and remote sensing. The cartographic model used is based on the Turkish model and employs multi-criteria AHP analyses. The integration of natural and human factors that influence fire behavior, such as plant biomass, morphology, accessibility, and urbanization, is crucial. According to GIS analysis, the combination of these parameters indicates that 45.52% of the massif had a high fire risk in 2014, which is related to the significant fuel. Due to the severe degradation of the massif, this area was reduced by about 16% in 2020. These results are essential for forest managers to consider.

articleTitle: The Enhanced RBF-BFOA Network for Remote Sensing Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: One of the primary objectives of remote sensing data processing is to extract maximum relevant information for the user. Optimization plays a crucial role in computer science, especially in learning problems such as neural network training. In this paper, we introduce a new bio-inspired algorithm to optimize the classical Radial Basis Function neural network: the Bacterial Foraging Optimization Algorithm (BFOA). The proposed approach is first presented and described, followed by an enhanced algorithm through modification of the chemotactic step in BFOA. Subsequently, we assess and compare the performance of both approaches through various remote sensing image classifications. After different tests, it is found that the proposed approach is very robust and efficient.

articleTitle: Assessing Anthropogenic and Climate Change Threats to Archaeological Landscapes in Iraq Using Earth Observation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Iraq is among the five countries most vulnerable to climate change impacts. Its cultural landscapes and heritage are exposed to erosion, weathering, abandonment and, eventually, disappearance. An approach combining satellite and on-the-ground observations to investigate anthropogenic and climate change-related processes is being developed in the framework of the Italian National Research Council – UK Royal Society bilateral cooperation programme. The data analysis workflow capitalises on decades of Earth observation imagery, including declassified HEXAGON, Copernicus Sentinel-1 radar, Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-3 multispectral data. The goal is to delineate archaeological sites and ancient water systems (canals, water bodies, wells), and generate derived products (e.g. yearly change detection maps based on interferometric coherence and vegetation indices variation, zonation of areas impacted by dust storms) depicting occurred transformations, regional susceptibility and endangered heritage sites.

articleTitle: Groundwater Quality Assessments For Drinking Purposes Based On WQI And GIS In The Plain Of Tabelbala, South-West Algeria
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The degradation of the aquifer environment has increasingly become a matter of global significance. Recently, urban discharges of toxic chemicals and organic elements are constantly polluting the aquifers in our region, leading to eutrophication of the reservoirs. This effect becomes a global concern due to the dangerous impact that can have on public health. The current investigation aims to conduct a qualitative assessment of the groundwater in the aquifers of the Tabelbala plain using the GWQI method. A total of 176 boreholes is examined in this investigation, analyzing various physicochemical parameters such as EC, pH, main cations, and anions. The analysis of the collected data indicates that a significant portion of the total surface area, precisely 62.8%, falls under the category of poor water quality. This area is primarily located in the center (Chraîa) and west of the study area. Additionally, around 18.15% of the surface area is classified as very poor quality, which is mainly observed in the village of Tabelbala and north of Charai. Furthermore, it should be noted that the northeastern part of the plain is characterized by a good water class, which accounts for over 12% of the total surface area. Conversely, the southern part of the plain is particularly prevalent in the non-potable class, which covers 6.34% of the total surface area. The use of remote sensing and GIS technology has produced outcomes that can be employed as a precautionary measure to prevent the consumption of water from regions with inferior quality and ensuring the security of individuals.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Forest Degradation Using Google Earth Engine (case study forest of Sidi Bel Abbes)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Cloud-computing engine using various classification techniques that include Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and algorithms to produce a multi-date land use land cover map of forest Sidi Bel Abbes region (2000-2020). Landsat images (ETM+ and OLI) will be used for the thematic classification of forest formations. The outcome demonstrated a reliable GEE-based mapping of the region’s forest with satisfactory classification accuracy. It revealed the overall accuracy values and the Kappa coefficients to be above 77% during the different time nodes under study. The research further revealed that the Random Forest performed the best machine-learning models tested in this study for mapping the forest and other land cover classes. At the end of this work, change maps will be drawn up. This approach will enable us to detect spatiotemporal changes in the forest landscape, establish conversion relationships between different land-use categories, and determine the direction, speed, and rate of land-use change for each defined period. This work will provide forest managers and other stakeholders with a decision-making tool that will enable them to plan the efficient and sustainable management and development of their respective areas.

articleTitle: Flood Risk Assessment Using Hydraulic Modeling and Remote Sensing Data: A Case Study of the M’zab Valley, (Algeria)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The objective of the present work is to create a geospatial map that assesses the risk of flooding in the Oud M’zab region, by integrating various parameters derived from remote sensing data (soil and land use land cover) and multi-source data (including topography, hydrographic networks, and lithology). Flooding is a significant concern in various sectors, including industrial, urbanization, hydraulic works, and road structures. This study focuses on hydrological modelling approaches to simulate flooding areas in the Oued M’zab region, bases on a peak flow and recorded flood data to obtain a preliminary assessment of potential flooding.In order to validate the hydrological consistency of this work, the HEC-RAS 1D tools were employed. The result of this analysis revealed four flood risk classes, ranging from low to high risk. The risk of flooding is particularly higher in the area where the banks and the river-beds are occupied by the urban population, while it tends to decrease while moving away from Oued and valley.

articleTitle: Detecting Local Crisis Events: A Case Study on the Colorado Wildfires through Social Media and Satellite Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Social media has become vital for disseminating natural disaster information, but its reliance has limitations. This study underscores the crucial integration of diverse data sources, particularly remote sensing and social sensing, to overcome challenges faced by traditional uni-modal methods. Using the Colorado wildfire as a case study, we applied advanced techniques, including named entity recognition and natural language processing, to extract tweet locations, grouping them based on geographical relevance. To enrich satellite imagery, we extracted images from tweet URLs, associating them with relevant tweet groups. This research combines theoretical and practical insights, addressing detection challenges within a simplified framework. It highlights the innovative integration of social media and satellite imagery, offering valuable directions for disaster response and management. This research aims to make the linkage between social media data and remote sensing data more clear to researchers. Specifically, it aims to enrich satellite imagery with images and text from tweets to provide a clearer view of events and their locations.

articleTitle: Effective Prediction of Global Solar Radiation Using Machine Learning Algorithms and Satellite Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Accurate prediction of Daily Global Solar Radiation (DGSR) is of prime importance for various applications in renewable energy, agriculture or climate studies. This paper presents the effectiveness of using Machine Learning (ML) algorithms and satellite imagery to improve DGSR prediction. The most commonly used ML methods consider as input the use of several meteorological parameters (temperature, wind speed, atmospheric pressure, sunshine duration, etc.) and/or radiometric parameters (aerosol optical thickness, water vapor, etc). In this work, the use of normalized reflectance obtained from satellite images in different channels is studied with the aim of improving the accuracy of solar radiation forecasts. Both ML approaches, ANN (Artificial Neural Network) and SVM (Support Vector Machine), were used as regression models to predict DGSR. The obtained results revealed that the number of parameters used as ML inputs significantly influences the accuracy of daily forecasts of global solar radiation. Furthermore, the results showed superior performance of ANN compared to SVM. Indeed, the errors obtained with the ANN model are an RMSE of 212.21 Wh/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, an NRMSE of 3.46%, a MAPE of 2.85%, an MBE of -7.26Wh/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and R of 0.99 while the SVM model gave respectively 441.95Wh/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 6.6%, 5.62%, 69.46W h/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and R of 0.98.

articleTitle: Spatial Estimation of Surface Soil Texture Using Machine Learning and Google Earth Engine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Land management, modeling, and monitoring require knowledge about the distribution of soil properties across the landscape. The main objective of this study is to use a combination of remote sensing data and machine learning techniques to estimate surface soil texture properties (sand, silt, and clay) in the northeastern region of Libya. The results showed that the coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) ranges between 0.39 and 0.48. The Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) varies from 5.04 to 8.28, while the Normalized Root Mean Square Error (NRMSE) ranges from 0.14 to 0.15. These values indicate that there is less residual variance. Therefore, the machine learning model was used correctly. These results demonstrate that the approach used for modeling and spatial mapping soil texture properties in this region is practical and valid. Furthermore, this methodology can be applied to other areas with similar characteristics.

articleTitle: Temporal Analysis of NDVI, Carbon Monoxide, and Land Cover Correlation in the Algerian Territory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Urbanization is often associated with an increase in human activity, transport, and energy consumption, leading to higher carbon monoxide emissions on the one hand, but also a reduction in green spaces due to the building, road, and infrastructure constructions.The work presented in this article consists of a temporal analysis of the relationship between NDVI, carbon monoxide, and land occupation in Algeria.The study used five years of Sentinel-5P data to calculate carbon monoxide emissions, and MODIS data to calculate the NDVI index.The results of the temporal analysis showed that NDVI and carbon monoxide have an opposite correlation. This means that the greater the amount of vegetation, the less carbon monoxide there is in the air.

articleTitle: Contribution of a Multitemporal Study Using Landsat Satellite Data in Land Cover Mapping of the Region of Bir El Djir in Oran, Algeria
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Algeria is a fast-developing country, whose economy and population are in constant growth. The changes are especially apparent in its urban and vegetation landscapes. The aim of this study is to map the spatio-temporal evolution of land cover in the region of Bir El Djir situated in Oran, Algeria. Knowing that the city of Oran is considered one of the biggest in the country. The proposed methodology relies on a pair of remote sensing data (Landsat TM and OLI TIRS images) acquired in 1987 and 2014 extending over a 27-year period. A diachronic analysis of these images was carried out on the basis of a supervised classification using a colored composition for class discrimination. The overall accuracy of the obtained classification results is equal to 93.15% and 90.60% for 1987 and 2014 respectively. The high quality obtained classes highlight with a good precision the dynamic changes within the area of study. As a result, we were able to establish that the dynamic change in land covers within Bir El Djir is closely related to the remoteness from the city center and main roads.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approach to LULC Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: This study explores the prediction of changes in Land Use and Land Cover (LULC) over the period of 2000 to 2040 in a region of Algeria. The research combines remote sensing data and machine learning techniques. Landsat image classification is applied to assess LULC changes for the years 2000 to 2020. In addition, a novel approach is employed to account for temporal factors influencing LULC changes in 2025, 2030, and 2040. Promising results are reported and discussed.

articleTitle: CLEXIDRA: Soil Moisture Retrieval on Crop Fields by Integration of Multi-Source Earth Observation data and Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: An automatic soil moisture retrieval algorithm from Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) over agricultural bare and vegetated fields is investigated. The work is carried out in the framework of the CLEXIDRA project funded by the Italian Space Agency (ASI).Soil moisture retrieval is based on (i) multi-frequency and polarimetric SAR data in L- (SAOCOM), X- (COSMO-SkyMed both First and Second generation) and C-band (Sentinel-1) integration (ii) bare and vegetated soil scattering models inversion; (iii) Bayesian minimization and machine learning techniques; (iv) biomass estimation from hyperspectral and multi-spectral electro-optical data; (v) ground-truth data collected over crop fields located in Argentina (Monte Buey) and in Northern Italy (Jolanda di Savoia). The proposed soil moisture detection algorithm is implemented for precision agricultural applications, thus enabling SAR products of soil moisture in agricultural irrigation management systems, as well as in global weather models for environmental monitoring purposes.

articleTitle: Dual-POL SLC and GRD Scattering Power Components for Land Cover Characterization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Scattering power components extracted from polarimetric SAR data have proven invaluable in characterizing diverse land cover targets. However, methods to derive the scattering powers are limited to full-polarimetric SAR data. This study introduces a novel approach to obtain scattering power components from dual-pol SLC and GRD SAR data. We assess the scattering power components observed over various land covers with Sentinel-1 image acquired over Buenos Aires, Argentina; Chennai, India; and Oran, Algeria. The proportion of the scattering powers varies depending upon the target’s physical and geometrical properties, which helps in their improved characterization.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Machine Learning Models to Predict the Probability of Forest Fires with Small Training Sample, Case of the Wilaya of Sidi Belabbes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The aim of this study is to evaluate machine learning models for predicting forest fire probability, based on 14 topographical, meteorological, anthropological and vegetation factors. A history of forest fires in the wilaya of Sidi Bel Abbes was used as a learning base, comprising 159 fire points. Eight models were tested, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Logistic Regression (LR), HistGradient Boosting Regressor (HGBR), Ada Boost Classifier (ABC), Gradient Boosting Classifier (GBC), Neural Network (NN), Gaussian Process Classifier (GPC). The Random Forest model posted the highest accuracy score, reaching 86.46%. The most influential factors in prediction were the median temperature and the Canadian Fire weather index (FWI).

articleTitle: Evaluation of Different Color Space Models for Estimation of Nitrate and Phosphate in Soil and Water Using a Smartphone-Integrated Imaging Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: To regulate agricultural inputs and monitor environmental pollution, this study offers a smartphone-integrated imaging device to quantify nitrate $\left( {{\text{N}}{{\text{O}}_3}^ - } \right)$ and phosphate $\left( {{\text{P}}{{\text{O}}_4}^{3 - }} \right)$ in soil and water samples. Using a smartphone’s digital camera, this cheap and portable device takes an image of the extracted solution being tested. The HSV color space model’s Value (V) component of the images was used to estimate the amounts of ${\text{N}}{{\text{O}}_3}^ -$ and ${\text{P}}{{\text{O}}_4}^{3 - }$ in soil and water samples. The limit of detection of the device for soil ${\text{N}}{{\text{O}}_3}^ -$, water ${\text{N}}{{\text{O}}_3}^ -$, soil phosphate, and water phosphate were calculated as 0.1 mg L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, 0.07 mg L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, 0.001 mg L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, and 0.02 mg L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, respectively, with good accuracy (≤1% bias) and precision (~2% residual standard deviation). Furthermore, to offer comparable results for the estimation of ${\text{N}}{{\text{O}}_3}^ -$ and ${\text{P}}{{\text{O}}_4}^{3 - }$ in soil and water, all the indices of the RGB, CMYK, and CIELAB color space models were examined and compared with the V-model. This cost-effective and user-friendly device provides reliable measurements comparable to a regular spectrophotometer.

articleTitle: InSAR-Based Assessment of Land Subsidence Related to Aquifer Overexploitation in Spain: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: In the upcoming years, global urban growth will drive increased water demand in urban and agricultural areas, while climate change will affect water resource timing and distribution. Groundwater, a crucial resource in many Mediterranean and Middle-Eastern countries, faces significant pressure as it is exploited at a higher rate than it can be recharged. Synthetic Aperture Radar Interferometry (InSAR) is widely employed for monitoring land subsidence due to the overexploitation of detrital aquifers. Utilizing InSAR as an Earth Observation (EO) technique offers advantages like high spatial density, extensive coverage, precision, and all-weather data collection. This work reviews InSAR data usage in studying groundwater-induced land subsidence, focusing on Spanish case studies by the Geohazards InSARlab team (IGME-CSIC).
