It showcases four instances where such data have contributed to modeling aquifer deformation and groundwater flow, and developing sustainable water management plans.

articleTitle: Automatic Detection and Extraction Framework of Ground Control Points for Remotely Sensed Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: In remote sensing applications particularly, the Ground Control Points (GCPs) are not always available for the purpose of image processing. Indeed, in inaccessible regions, traditional methods of acquiring accurate GCPs, such as ground surveying or GPS measurements, may not be feasible. Identifying GCPs in difficult-to-reach areas can pose significant challenges due to limited ground access and logistical constraints. This study introduces an alternative method for automating the detection and extraction of GCPs from remote-sensing satellite imagery. The method consists of two main phases: Data pre-processing and GCPs identification and extraction. In the first phase, the study focuses on enhancing image quality by utilizing band selection and contrast enhancement techniques. In the second phase, the identification and extraction of GCPS is established by combining SURF and SIFT algorithms. The proposed framework is tested to ALSAT2 satellite images in challenging scenarios. These findings indicate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately identifying and extracting GCPs for remote sensing satellite imagery. The findings show a 36.5% rise in the quantity of identified GCPs using the proposed technique in contrast to the traditional SURF algorithm across all datasets.

articleTitle: CubeSat for IEEE-GRSS Algeria Chapter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: A CubeSat is a class of satellite that follows a standardized size and shape known as a 'U'. Specifically, a 1U CubeSat is a 10 cm cube with a maximum weight of 2 kg. CubeSats provide affordable access to space for small companies, research institutes and universities. They are mainly launched into low Earth orbit for applications such as remote sensing, space weather measurements and communications. Many educational CubeSat based projects have been created for research purposes and education in institutes and universities. In this way, the IEEE-GRSS via the IEEE-MENA region supported some chapters to acquire CubeSat to provide scientific community with educational tool permitting to train, develop and test space technology activities on ground. The IEEE-GRSS Algeria chapter has started exploiting the different functionalities of the CubeSat from its control in the earth segment to the space via its communication system. The cube sat components have been successfully assembled, set up and putted into operation. Many simulations using a laptop endowed with ground segment software have been tested and resulted in a complete handling of the Educational SATellite (ESAT). The chapter team responsible of the system, has also created educational and industrial partnerships to share knowledge to understand well ESAT functionalities and try to develop other elements for further applications.

articleTitle: Understanding the Topography of the Gulf of Guinea Seabed Using GMT Scripting and GEBCO Gridded Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The seabed topography of the Gulf of Guinea is still largely unexplored, despite being a vital and dynamic maritime region. By utilising GMT (Generic Mapping Tools) scripting in conjunction with GEBCO (General Bathymetric Chart of the Oceans) gridded data, this study revealed the complex topography of this region. A thorough analysis and visualisation of the bottom topography of the Gulf of Guinea are sought after through the combination of these potent instruments. The purpose of this study is to reveal the complex geological features, and comprehend changes in underwater topography. Through the use of GMT scripting, the study presents a strong approach for modifying and analysing GEBCO gridded data, offering a more thorough comprehension of the intricate and varied undersea environment in the Gulf of Guinea. The results have significant implications for a number of fields, such as resource management in this vital maritime region, environmental conservation, and marine exploration.

articleTitle: Remote Sensing and in-Situ Data for Urban Heat Island Characterization in Oran City
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: This study addresses the Urban Heat Island (UHI) characterization of Oran agglomeration with the aim of modeling the link between the Land Surface Temperature (LST) previously restituted from the analysis of Landsat satellite images and air temperatures. The results obtained show that the vegetation cover, characterized by NDVI, has a significant influence on the LST, which is considered as a reliable indicator of the UHI. The warmest areas are usually found in dense intra-urban areas and industrial zones. The exploitation of the free data mining software Rattle (graphical interface for data mining using the R software), and the artificial neural networks with multiple linear regression, led to modeling the relationship between surface temperature and air temperature.

articleTitle: Application Of Remote Sensing Data In Lithological Discrimination Of Gypsum In Tataouine Area, Southern Tunisia
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The abstract focuses on the application of remote sensing data for lithological discrimination in the Tataouine area of southern Tunisia, with a specific emphasis on gypsum of the Mestaoua formation [1], that constitutes the 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> reserve worldwide. It highlights the relevance of remote sensing data due to their spatial, spectral, and radiometric characteristics, which are crucial for accurate lithological mapping and mineral exploration. The research project is part of the larger REMINT project led by the National Center for Cartography and Remote Sensing.Various spectral and radiometric transformations, including band ratios, spectral indices, principal components analysis (PCA), and independent components analysis (ICA), were applied to ASTER data to enhance lithological discrimination and delineation between outcropping formations [2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9] in the study area. The results of these methods were compared with existing geological and field investigations, demonstrating their effectiveness in mapping lithological units.Notably, band ratios derived from the image spectra were utilized in two RGB color composites, namely (4/2, 4+6/5, 7/6) and (4+6/5, 7/6, 8/7), successfully discriminating lithological units such as the gypsum of the Mestaoua formation, Aeolian sand covers, clay, and sandstone of the Techout formation.The research findings provide valuable insights into the lithological composition of the Tataouine area, particularly regarding gypsum. These outcomes significantly contribute to the field of lithological mapping and mineral exploration. Furthermore, they demonstrate the potential of remote sensing data for identifying and characterizing mineral resources in similar regions. These results are significant for proving the great potential of ASTER data, which was downloaded free from the USGS site, in lithological discrimination and for opening a new avenue for lithological mapping using remote sensing data.

articleTitle: Constraints On Soil Moisture Extraction From Sentinel-1
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: A comparison between the Sentinel-1 (S1)/Sentinel-2 (S2) derived Soil Moisture Products at plot scale (S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>MP) and in situ soil moisture measurements at 10 cm depth was carried out for several winter and summer crops (wheat, tomato, cover crops and soybeans) with the aim to provide end users with the strength and limitations of the S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>MP soil moisture product for their further applications. In dry conditions, the estimated S1 soil moisture (SM) (at ~5 cm depth) highly underestimated the 10 cm SM measurements. Wet conditions due to rainfall or irrigation showed less difference between the S1 estimated SM and the 10 cm in situ SM. Comparison of S1 estimated SM as a function of the vegetation development showed that for the studied crop types the S1 SM estimates are only valid for low and moderate vegetation cover with Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) less than 0.7. Results also suggested that the optimal SM estimations by S1 could be mainly obtained at low radar incidence angles.

articleTitle: Boreal biome wetland classification using multi-seasonal EO data on gee and machine learning optimization/XAI modelling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The objective of this study was to map wetlands representing 2017-2022 conditions in two areas in Canada’s Boreal Forest, specifically Nunavut’s taiga shield ecozone and Saskatchewan’s boreal shield ecozone. Wetland classification was performed by leveraging machine learning (ML) modelling on the Google Earth Engine (GEE) JavaScript API, and Python programming for model cross validation/optimization and explainbility. Robust wetland coverage estimates were derived by summarizing the predictions of several ML models (i.e., an ensemble) trained on different sample subsets. Moreover, this study employed two key components to improve the wetland mapping modelling: (1) the processing of multi-temporal, multiseasonal (summer and fall) satellite imagery, since timeseries observations capture shifting eco-hydrological conditions, and (2) the use of Grey Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) textural variables, which are understudied in the GEE literature. Models were interpreted using Shapley explainable AI (XAI) methods. Overall accuracies of > 95% suggest this is a promising methodology.

articleTitle: Analysis and Assessment of Changes in Land use and Land Degradation in The Steppes Using Spatial Tools: A Case Study of the Naama Region
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: In recent years, the steppe rangelands have suffered severe degradation due to the combined effects of human and natural pressure. This deterioration can be seen in the decline in vegetation cover, the disappearance of certain species, the intensive silting up of agricultural and non-agricultural land and the appearance of large bare areas, preparing the soil for harmful wind and water erosion. Faced with this situation. However, it is essential to be able to analyze and assess the vegetation cover and the extent of the sands, in order to identify problem areas (degradation).The aim of this study is to show the contribution of remote sensing and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) in mapping changes in land use and the degradation of agricultural land in the steppe region of Naama between 1987 and 2019.The method used is based on digital processing of multi-date images from Landsat 5 and 8 sensors (supervised classification and calculation of TS soil temperature).The results of this work show an increase in agricultural land and psammophyte trails. The surface area of bare soil and esparto trails, on the other hand, has declined as a result of silting and overgrazing.

articleTitle: Soil Moisture Mapping Using Gnss-R and L-Band Microwave Radiometry: Instruments and Techniques Developed at UPC-Barcelonatech
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Soil Moisture (SM) is one of the Essential Climate Variables (ECVs) needed to better understand the water cycle, to assess climate change, and it is crucial to monitor floods and droughts, in agriculture, etc. SM mapping at large scale is only feasible using remote sensing sensors for Earth observation. In this paper, the different soil moisture mapping techniques are first revised, then SM mapping using L-band microwave radiometers and GNSS-Reflectometers are presented using UPC-developed techniques and airborne and spaceborne instruments. Downscaled SM mapping techniques are described in detail in the companion paper by Pablos et al. titled "Two disaggregation algorithms to estimate soil moisture at moderate (1 km and 300 m) and at high (60 m) resolution: Applications over the North of Africa" presented also at this conference.

articleTitle: Iterative Music for Single-Look Sar Tomography
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: This paper proposes an iterative adaptation of the Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) algorithm for single-look tomographic Synthetic Aperture Radar reconstruction. Our primary objective is to adapt MUSIC for single-look scenarios to deal with the spatial resolution degradation associated with multi-look processing. Compared to the spatial smoothing approach proposed in the literature, a key advantage of our method is its independence from requiring a uniform baseline. Consequently, there is no need for sector interpolation to make the baseline uniform. The proposed method begins with an initialization using the pseudo-spectrum derived from matched spatial filtering. The latter is enhanced through a series of iterative steps, resulting in substantial resolution improvements. Numerical simulations confirm the superior performances of our method compared to state-of-the-art iterative approaches.

articleTitle: Integrating Texture Features with a Weighted Differential Evolution Algorithm for Satellite Image Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Satellite image data classification is crucial for categorizing pixels into meaningful classes. While traditional reliance on spectral information has limitations, a shift to textural features from the co-occurrence matrix proves essential. This paper introduces the Weighted Differential Evolution Algorithm (WDEA) for numerical optimization, focusing on CHI, XB, and DBI indices. The evaluation includes Partitioning Around Medoids (PAM) and Hierarchical Centroid (HC) methods. Comparisons with the K-means (KM) algorithm confirm the effectiveness of WDEA in satellite image clustering.

articleTitle: Addressing Spectral Variability in Hyperspectral Unmixing with a Novel Linear Adaptive Additive Mixing Model and an Associated ADMM-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Spectral variability often affects remote sensing hyperspectral data, presenting challenges for their unmixing process when considering the traditional linear mixing model, which ignores such an issue. Consequently, more advanced linear mixing models, which address this phenomenon, need to be considered. In this work, an original linear adaptive additive mixing model is proposed to deal with spectral variability. It considers this concern in the spectral part of the manipulated variables. In addition, an associated unmixing algorithm, based on an alternating direction method of multipliers framework, is designed for the proposed model. The usefulness of this algorithm is clearly proven by outcomes of experiments carried out with synthetic data.

articleTitle: Impact of Temperature Perturbation on the Atmospheric Instability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The increase in anthropogenic activities due to large-scale urbanization and industrialization causes unprecedented changes in atmospheric conditions. Several studies reported anthropogenic emissions and their impact on air quality. However, fewer attempts are made to investigate the impact of temperature change due to anthropogenic activity on the Atmospheric Boundary Layer (ABL) and atmospheric instability processes. In this present study, the impact of temperature perturbation due to anthropogenic heating on atmospheric instability (Convective Available Potential Energy (CAPE) and Convective Inhibition Energy (CIN)) is studied exclusively by using the WRF model. Two main CAPE seasons are identified in the study. A high value of CAPE is observed in the monsoon season, and a low CAPE is observed in the pre-monsoon season. Even if a lower value of CAPE does not guarantee deep moist convection in pre-monsoon as more CIN is present.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Land Cover with Satellite Images from Landsat 8, Sentinel 1 and the Random Forest Algorithm in the Municipality of Villanueva Casanare
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: SUMMARYSoils are a basic requirement for meeting human needs, but human pressure on soil resources is reaching critical limits. Anthropogenic effects, soil contamination and monocultures pose major challenges for sustainable soil management. In Colombia, the significant increase in oil palm monocultures has generated different changes in soil use, alterations in ecosystems and greater vulnerability in food security. This is the case of the municipality of Villanueva Casanare where oil palm planting has been increasing since 1988, displacing other crops with higher occupancy such as rice, which contributes to improve the food security of the population. This research aims to evaluate land cover with satellite images of Landsat 8, Sentinel 1 and the Random Forest algorithm in Villanueva Casanare for the year 2019. For this purpose, a supervised classification was performed for the Landsat 8 optical sensor and for the Sentinel 1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), with a training of 7 classes (Forests, Pastures, Water Bodies, Urban Areas, Oil Palm, Other Crops and Bare Soils) that summarize the coverages of the Municipality of Villanueva Casanare, The corresponding reflectance and Spackle corrections were made, then the two supervised classifications were merged and run through the Random forest algorithm, likewise a confusion matrix was performed to corroborate the accuracy, all of the above in the Google Earth Engine platform. As main results of the three methods used with the Random Forest algorithm, the one with the highest accuracy of the seven proposed classes is the combination of SAR and Landsat 8, due to its 99.95% accuracy in the different coverages analyzed in the municipality of Villanueva Casanare.

articleTitle: Two Disaggregation Algorithms to Estimate Soil Moisture at Moderate (1 km and 300 m) and at High Resolution (60 m): Applications over the North of Africa
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The Barcelona Expert Center (BEC) has become an international reference in the generation of high resolution soil moisture (SM) maps using disaggregation algorithms. More than a decade ago, a semi-empirical approach was developed to produce Soil Moisture and Ocean Salinity (SMOS) SM at 1 km. This method has been refined over the years to obtain cloud free maps, and modified to further improve the spatial resolution up to 300 m. More recently, a machine-learning approach has been developed to derive European Space Agency (ESA)’s Climate Change Initiative (CCI) SM at 60 m.Thanks to the multi-spectral information added during the disaggregation process, the downscaled SM maps have an overall accuracy similar to the coarse ones, but provide additional information about the SM spatial variability. In this regard, three different applications over the north of Africa are presented here to exemplify the added-value of SM data at high resolution.

articleTitle: Post-Flood Disaster Mapping Using Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: This work proposes an efficient approach for post-flood disaster change detection in the Derna region, Libya, utilizing a pair of Sentinel-2 images captured before and after the flood disaster. A dataset was generated by pairing these two temporally distinct images of the same scene, each composed of four spectral bands, with a corresponding label image indicating change or no change for each region of interest. This dataset was then fed into a custom-designed deep neural network (DNN) for change classification. The DNN was trained on this data to automatically identify and map areas that had undergone changes following the disaster. This method effectively combines the potential of Sentinel-2 images and deep learning to facilitate precise and automated post-disaster change detection, thereby contributing to emergency assessment and management.

articleTitle: Shapley Explainable AI (XAI) to Assess the Potential of Satellite Remote Sensing Data for Estimating Active Layer Thickness (ALT)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Permafrost environments are increasingly threatened by warming temperatures. Active Layer Thickness (ALT) is a critical variable because it influences several environmental processes, particularly carbon storage and cycling. Remote Sensing (RS) techniques hold great potential for mapping ALT over remote, challenging, and inaccessible permafrost regions, especially in comparison to in situ field surveys. In this study, various RS sources (radar, optical, topographic) were assessed for ALT estimation. ALT samples were obtained from airborne radar imaging (P- and L-Band) through the NASA Arctic Boreal Vulnerability Experiment (ABoVE), and then upscaled to satellite observations using machine learning (ML) modelling. Using Explainable AI (XAI) methods, we provide interpretation of our ML modeling by assessing the relevance of 116 input RS features. The Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) XAI method was utilized for this interpretation task. Temperature and topography features provided the greatest explanation in ALT variability. Therefore, this study provides insight into the potential of satellite RS for estimating ALT, and the relative importance of RS features for this challenging task.

articleTitle: Quantum Annealing for Semantic Segmentation in Remote Sensing: Potential and Limitations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Quantum Annealing (QA) is a powerful method for combinatorial optimization derived from adiabatic quantum computation. The development of computing devices implementing QA accelerated its adoption in practical use cases. In this paper, we summarize the main features and limitations of QA and its application to remote sensing, specifically to semantic segmentation. We provide indications for successfully applying it to real problems, and techniques for improving its performance. This overview can support practitioners in the adoption of this innovative computing technology.

articleTitle: Utilising Declassified Cold War Satellite Imagery (KH-9 Hexagon) for Remote Sensing of Historic Hydraulic Management Features in North Africa
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Since its declassification by the United States in 1995, imagery from Cold War Era (1947-1991) satellite programmes has become a powerful remote sensing tool. The scientific community has employed this imagery for a multitude of environmental and landscape studies since it became publicly available. Archaeologists first utilised imagery from the CORONA programme to locate unrecorded archaeological sites in the Middle East and have continued its use elsewhere. The final Cold War satellite programme, KH-9, codenamed HEXAGON (1971-1986), was declassified in 2011 but made publicly available from the United States Geological Survey (USGS) in 2022. The characteristics of HEXAGON imagery make it a better tool than CORONA for cultural heritage studies, especially those that wish to document landscape and site change. This paper presents a brief overview of a methodology to accurately orthorectify the KH-9 imagery and the documentation of traditional water management features such as the underground abstraction galleries (khettara) in Skoura Oasis, Morocco.

articleTitle: SAR Observation Data-Driven Geohazard Monitoring in Algeria: Utilizing DInSAR and MT-InSAR Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: This paper presents different applications of DInSAR and MT-InSAR for assessing ground deformation in Algeria. Case studies across the country using Sentinel-1 SAR data are shown for measuring surface deformation related to seismic events, analyzing infrastructure health monitoring, urban subsidence, and sinkhole hazards. Results include coseismic displacement maps for the 2016 Zeribet El Oued and 2020 Mila earthquakes. Time series analysis is applied to monitor displacements at the Kramis dam and to quantify subsidence rates in the OKN32 crater. Mean velocity maps generated from Envisat and Sentinel-1 highlight subsidence patterns in Oran city. This work demonstrates the value of SAR interferometry for mapping and monitoring different types of ground instability phenomena in Algeria.

articleTitle: Mapping Agricultural Greenhouses in Algeria: A Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Agricultural Greenhouses (AGs) are increasingly crucial in global food security, particularly in arid and semi-arid regions like the Maghreb, where they offer sustainable solutions to water scarcity and climate change challenges. Despite their growing importance, the precise extent and distribution of AGs in these regions remain poorly mapped, largely due to the limitations of traditional survey methods and the diverse nature of AG infrastructures. This study introduces a novel, deep learning-based approach to map AGs in the Maghreb, focusing on a 20-year case study in Biskra, Algeria (2000-2024). Employing remote sensing with Landsat imagery and the U-Net deep learning architecture, this research aims to provide a detailed, temporal mapping of AGs, offering insights into their dynamics and informing sustainable agricultural policies in the region.

articleTitle: Object-Based Cereal Crop Mapping Using Sentinel-2 Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: This study investigates the possibilities of improving the cereal crop mapping on high spatial resolution images by using object-based approach, superpixel segmentation and the Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) texture. The proposed approach was implemented on Google Earth Engine (GEE) which provides a fast and easy-to-use platform with its freely available datasets and geospatial analysis tools for applications such classification. In this study, Multispectral Instrument (MSI) images of Sentinel-2 were utilized to classify cropland area of Sidi Bel Abbes city. The obtained results were validated by ground truth samples relative to cereal growing period (may 2021).

articleTitle: Optimizing for Edge-AI Based Satellite Image Processing: A Survey of Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Higher autonomy in satellite operations is considered a significant game-changer for the space systems market in the coming decade, with numerous agencies and startups focusing on integrating machine learning into space technology. However, the adoption of artificial intelligence onboard satellites is limited by computational resources and power constraints. Therefore, AI researchers have developed several optimization techniques and tools to optimize AI models deployed on the edge. This survey reviews techniques and strategies for optimizing AI models for satellite edge deployment, including hardware acceleration, lightweight models, and compression techniques. It serves as a comprehensive reference and a starting point for further research into optimizing satellite EdgeAI deployment.

articleTitle: Efficient UAV-Borne Hyperspectral Image Classification Using Spatial Guided Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: This paper introduces a spectral and spatial classification approach specifically tailored for high spatial resolution UAV-borne hyperspectral remote sensing imagery. The proposed approach combines a support vector machine (SVM) classifier with a guided image filter to effectively utilize both spectral and spatial features. The guided filter is employed to extract spatial information and optimize classification results. Empirical results demonstrate a significant improvement in overall accuracy within a reasonable timeframe. These findings highlight the effectiveness of the proposed approach in enhancing classification accuracy, particularly in the context of Land Use and Land Cover applications (LULC). By leveraging the synergy between the SVM classifier and guided image filter, the method provides a practical solution for high spatial resolution hyperspectral image classification. Future investigations should focus on expanding the training dataset and assessing the classifier’s performance on diverse hyperspectral images to enhance its adaptability and generalization capabilities.

articleTitle: Fully Convolutional Network-Based Change Detection in Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The technological progress in the computer vision field along with the new generations of space borne remote sensing sensors has revolutionized the remote sensing science, especially in change detection task. In this investigation, a fully convolutional neural network-based remote sensing images change detection framework is introduced. The proposed approach is an unsupervised one, which exploits the features extracted from different layers of a deep neural network without pooling layers. The evaluation of this approach is performed using pair of images from the ONERA change detection dataset, by considering established performance criteria. These experiments show very promising quantitative and visual results provided by the proposed approach, and illustrate its efficiency for change detection in urban and agricultural areas.

Author Keywords: transfer learning and fully convolutional neural networks

articleTitle: Sensitivity of Microphysical Schemes to Predict Induced Rainfall
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: In the present study, numerical simulation is carried out in the mesoscale Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) platform to determine the best set of physics options for better prediction of hydrometers to capture industrial effects. Angul region (20.85ºN, 85.19ºE) in Odisha state is chosen as the study region for this purpose since the region houses a lot of industries. A comparative study is done with different microphysics (MP) options available in the WRF model. From this sensitivity study, it has been found WDM6 based MP scheme is better at predicting industry-induced rainfall.

articleTitle: Development of an Advanced Tool for the Automatic Detection and Correction of Irregular Defects in Raw Satellite Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a robust tool for automatically detecting and correcting irregular defects in unprocessed satellite imagery, including erroneous or corrupted pixels, lines, and columns. The tool ensures the quality of the resulting data by removing defects while preserving the integrity and detail of the original image. Additionally, the tool's outputs enable operators and image quality analysts to swiftly identify the nature of these errors, whether temporary, random, or permanent, and determine their origins, such as optical payload failures, image acquisition or data transmission issues, data storage problems, electromagnetic interference, or environmental disturbances. The tool's results guarantee the reliability of the corrected data, ready for further processing and analysis.

articleTitle: Active Hyperspectral-Based Projects at the Algerian Space Agency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: This paper describes some ongoing projects at the Algerian Space Agency that utilize remote sensing hyperspectral data, with a special emphasis on those acquired from the spaceborne PRISMA sensor. These investigations, fostered through both national and international collaborations, are divided into two categories: methodological advancements in hyperspectral data processing and the development of space applications predominantly using such advanced methods. The methodological advancements primarily focus on unsupervised and informed unmixing techniques, which incorporate both linear and non-linear mixing models, without or with taking into account the spectral variability phenomenon, and also the sharpening of considered data using the unmixing concept. As for the space applications, they are mainly oriented towards sectors such as mineral prospecting, monitoring of urban and marine environments, and the detection and analysis of greenhouse gas emissions.

articleTitle: Automatic Desert Off-Road Track Mapping Using The Fusion Of Sentinel-2 And Prisma Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The ever-changing characteristics of desert tracks require consistent detection, and leveraging the advantages offered by remote sensing can address these challenges. This research focuses on mitigating spectral indistinctiveness exacerbated by dynamic landscapes. It tackles spatial limitations inherent to Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) by utilizing the spatial resolution of Sentinel-2 data and the heightened spectral sensitivity and spatial resolution of PRISMA data. This study introduces an automated framework that integrates Sentinel- 2 and PRISMA data to automatically map off-road tracks in desert environments. The proposed approach involves fusing Sentinel-2 RGB and Infrared bands with the panchromatic band of PRISMA data, thereby augmenting the number of samples for narrow tracks. Edge detection techniques (Laplacian and Canny) and the NDWI index are employed to distinguish drainage networks, refining the data for machine learning classifiers (Multilayer Perceptron and Random Forest). Validated against data from the INCT (Institut National de Cartographie et de Télédétection), the proposed system demonstrates good generalizability across new areas of interest, highlighting its potential in desert track mapping. The high accuracy achieved with the MLP (0.97) and RF (0.98) classifiers is noteworthy. However, false positives occur due to homogeneous desert landscapes, prompting the need for further refinement.

articleTitle: Contribution of C-Band Radar Data to the Description of Vegetation Dynamics in the Surface Soil Moisture Retrieval in Semi-Arid Region
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: To retrieve the surface soil moisture using the radar data, several works performed the inversion of the Water Cloud Model (WCM) where the Normalized Vegetation Difference Index (NDVI) was used as vegetation descriptor.In the case of cloud presence, the optical data availability is limited. Therefore, in the present work, we compared the potential of the NDVI and the cross-polarization ratio and its normalized index (IN) calculated from Sentinel-1 data to describe the wheat dynamic in the soil moisture retrieve process. After the calibration and the validation of WCM, the inversion results were characterized by RMSE values varying between 5.6 vol.% and 7.4 vol.% with the outperformance of the NDVI use. Relatively close accuracy characterized the estimation of soil moisture using the radar derived descriptors.

articleTitle: Mapping of Debris Cover with Thematic Indices and Mono-Window Algorithm Over Zemu Glacier in Sikkim Himalaya
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Zemu Glacier, a prominent glacier in the eastern Himalayas, remains largely unexplored in various glacier research endeavors. Satellite remote sensing and GIS techniques function as valuable tools for appraising temporal changes in remote glacial terrains that are challenging to reach. The scope of this study explores the distinguished prospective routes of automated mapping of glacial land cover using visible and thermal-infrared (TIR) bands of Landsat series along with the Mono-Window algorithm to calculate Glacial surface temperature (GST) for the spatial distribution of debris cover and Shuttle Radar Topographic Mission (SRTM) Digital Elevation Model (DEM) for slope and aspect. The temporal change analysis of debris-cover portrays more than 50% of the approximate change from the year 1989 to 2022.

articleTitle: Developing a Mapbasic-Driven Multicriteria Decision Support Tool for Environmental Management: A Case Study on the Selection of a Technical Landfill Site in Djelfa
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: In this study, we utilized the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and ELECTRE I methods for multicriteria analysis to determine the optimal location for a Sanitary Landfill (SL). The AHP method, known for its versatility and successful applications in various fields, provided a systematic approach to decomposing the problem, performing binary combinations, determining priorities, and synthesizing results. The integration of these methods into a Geographic Information System (GIS) involved careful consideration of three levels of physical integration, with a preference for complete integration for flexibility.The results obtained from the application of AHP and ELECTRE I methods were compared, revealing that AHP offered a clear ranking of site suitability, while ELECTRE I identified multiple favorable locations. Site 4 emerged consistently as the most favorable in both methods.In conclusion, the AHP method proved effective for decision-makers in urban planning, providing a structured approach to handling complex problems. However, the ELECTRE I method exhibited limitations in addressing uncertain and conflicting decisions. The integration of these methods into GIS enhances spatial analysis capabilities, contributing to advancements in decision support systems for waste management.

articleTitle: Application of the Daily Fire Danger index to Algerian Large Fire Events
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The Daily Fire Danger Index aims at providing a daily map of the areas where fire ignition and propagation is more likely. The paper shows the behavior of this index during a major fire event that affected Algeria in the summer of 2022. The increasing incidence of wildfires and megafires, both in terms of burnt area surface and in terms of power released by the fires, makes the strategic importance of prevention strategies and tools greater than ever. To this end, satellite observations offer a privileged platform to cover large spatial scales with a high time frequency. This paper aims at demonstrating the utility of a scalable-resolution fire danger index, named Daily Fire Danger Index, based on Sentinel-2 L2A and Sentinel-3 Synergy products for developing an operational system for wildfire prevention in Algeria. This index exploits both weather and satellite data to estimate all the main fire weather variables and is calibrated using the historical records of wildfire occurrence in the area of interest.

articleTitle: Contribution to the Development of an Optical Payload for an Educational Nanosatellite
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Nanosatellites have overcome the trial missions and become competitive solutions for various applications such as communication, remote sensing, navigation, etc. In this context, the ground should be prepared to promote this a new space trend in the local sectors that could contribute to the industrial aerospace ecosystem, i.e. the manufacturing sector, Algerian universities and companies that have the potential to exploit these new products. Through a training platform (PEDAGO-SAT) currently being developed at CDS, we propose an educational support tool for the academic community and researchers, intending in practice to approach development thematic of certain nanosatellite functionalities or applications (sensors, actuators, payloads, power system, attitude determination and control, etc.). this work is focusing on the payload side, proposing a preliminary architecture based on a low-cost imager intended to be embarked on this nanosatellite in order to cover, in laboratory, the processing of an optical mission, imaging, storing and down-link data via the radio frequency (RF) chain. This imaging system comprises a basic RGB camera managed by a front-end electronic module for image capture and a storage. The time tagging of image capture and downloading will be handled by onboard computer (OBC).

articleTitle: Italian Space Agency’s Scientific Downstream Applications from Multi-Frequency SAR to Hyperspectral Prisma Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: An overview of the applications that are currently developed based on multi-frequency Synthetic Aperture Radar and hyperspectral optical data is provided, in the context of the scientific downstream roadmap implemented by the Italian Space Agency (ASI). A selection of results is showcased, with particular reference to "Multi-mission and multi-frequency SAR", "PRISMA Scienza" and "Development of hyperspectral advanced prototype products" programs. The most emerging applications include precision farming, assessment of natural and anthropogenic hazards, water quality and forest monitoring.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical CNN Architecture for Semantic Segmentation of Radar Sounder Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The article presents for the first time a hybrid quantum-classical architecture in the context of subsurface target detection in the radar sounder signal. We enhance the classical convolutional neural network (CNN) based architecture by integrating a quantum layer in the latent space. We investigate two quantum circuits with the classical neural networks by exploiting fundamental properties of quantum mechanics such as entanglement and superposition. The proposed hybrid architecture is used for the downstream task of patch-wise semantic segmentation of radar sounder subsurface images. Experimental results on the MCoRDS and MCoRDS3 datasets demonstrated the capability of the hybrid quantum-classical approach for radar sounder information extraction.

articleTitle: Study of the Dynamics of Vegetation Through the Use of Vegetation Indices in the Region of Djelfa, Algeria
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The objective of this study is to propose an approach for monitoring the spatio-temporal evolution of land use in semi-arid steppe zones through the example of the Djelfa zone in Algeria over a period of 36 years. (1986-2021) and systematic sampling over 5 years (8 samples), as well as observation of the impact of climate and human activities on the natural plant cover.Three vegetation indices: NDVI, EVI, and MSAVI , were first calculated in the spring period, then aggregated by two methods: the Median, and the greenest pixel, to determine the composite mosaic images and the index best suited to describing the vegetation of the area.The results obtained showed that the MSAVI aggregated by the greenest pixel method presented the vegetation better than EVI and NDVI; And that there is a considerable degradation of the forest cover caused mainly by agriculture which increased; A degradation in steppe rangeland is also noted due to climatic degradation caused by a reduction in precipitation, and on the other hand the decline in steppe surface area, and overgrazing.

articleTitle: Investigating the Relationship Between SAR and Optical Data Indices for Cereal Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Continuous satellite data acquisition is essential for the effective crop monitoring. Unfortunately, optical data frequently relies on sunlight and weather conditions, prompting the utilization of complementary satellite data such as SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) data. In this context, our study aims to investigate the correlation between spectral indices employed in crop monitoring, specifically for cereal crops, like NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index), GNDVI (Green Normalized Difference Vegetation), EVI (enhanced vegetation Index), GCVI (green chlorophyll vegetation index), and NDWI (Normalized Difference Water Index), and the arithmetic combinations of amplitudes extracted from SAR data in VV and VH polarizations in order to ensure a time series for cereal crop monitoring. The experiments were conducted in the Sidi-Bel-Abbès region, yielding encouraging results.

articleTitle: SIFT and Gabor Based Features Extraction Method Applied to the Infrared VHR Image of Boumerdes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: This paper investigates the contribution of SIFT and Gabor features in the classification of a VHR Image, focusing on the Infrared and RGB channels. The assessment of the classification scheme is conducted by the SVM classifier, and the comparison using the average accuracy as a metric reveals that the infrared channel improves the performance of the classification scheme.

articleTitle: A Non-Stellar Big Bright Object Elimination and Star Centroid Extraction Algorithm for Star Tracker
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The star tracker is a highly accurate measuring instrument used in satellite attitude measurement and determination systems. Stellar images are important since they are the first key in the satellite attitude control process. In the lost-in-space case, stellar images are captured randomly by a star tracker, since the space environment does not only contain stars. Stellar images may include stars and even non-stellar objects. When the non-stellar big bright objects are present in the stellar images, the attitude calculation process might be challenging. This paper proposes a nonstellar big bright object elimination and star centroid calculation algorithm for a star tracker. On a set of generated stellar images, the suggested algorithm was tested. The results demonstrate the proposed algorithm's ability to remove the non-stellar big bright object's appearance and extract the star’s position from the stellar images.

articleTitle: Bangalore Coming Closer to It’s Satellite Town : Overview of Urban Sprawl in The City
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Urbanization is a worldwide phenomenon is much evident in 21<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> century. This widespread occurrence is mostly caused by infrastructure and economic growth followed by population expansion. Rapid urbanization with the changes in land use patterns has resulted in urban expansion that happens linearly in certain directions or radially around the city. The extent of urbanization, which is a global phenomenon mainly driven by population growth and large scale migration is referred as urban sprawl. Spatial metrics are used to quantify urban sprawl based on patch size, density, shapes etc. Spatial metrics quantified is computed on the entire built-up area of the city as metrics here is computed on the entire image and can be analyzed for any part of the city to be studied in details. The human induced urban heat island (UHI) is a well-known phenomenon in urban environment which is more evident in the cases of urban sprawl. City-heat interacts with rising summer temperatures and heat-waves, placing additional pressure on infrastructure. Landsat 8 dataset of 2014 and 2021 was used for the spatio-temporal analysis. This study focuses on summer season when UHI effect is apparent. Multiple ring buffer of 1 km radius was overlaid from the centre towards the periphery of the city to analyze the variations in Land Surface Temperature (LST) and sprawling pattern. It was found that the as we go away from the centre LST also increased that can be attributed to unplanned urbanization.

articleTitle: Using Multi-Date Prisma Satellite Data to Retrieve Topsoil Properties in Agricultural Fields: Spectra Selection from Surface Soil Moisture Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The estimation of topsoil properties such as texture and organic carbon (SOC), from satellite imaging spectroscopy is hampered by the variation of soil moisture at the time of data acquisition. In this work, a soil moisture estimation model is applied to PRISMA data, to select spectra acquired under dry conditions, from data collected in different dates in three study sites in Italy. The dataset is compared to one obtained by averaging the spectra acquired at different dates on the same elementary sampling units. The estimation of soil properties is performed using machine learning regression algorithms (MLRA). The selection of relatively dry spectra provided better results for the estimation of clay, for which a GPR model gave a relative root mean squared error (RRMSE) of 26.52. However, for sand and SOC the mean spectra from the different PRISMA acquisition dates provided better results.

articleTitle: Development of a Webgis for Cereal Lands Inventory City of Sidi-Bel-Abbes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: This article examines Web mapping technologies with an attention on architectures. Numerous Web GIS products from leading GIS sectors have been scientifically assessed. This paper presents an approach to Web mapping development, starting with a needs analysis and ending with GIS use and updating. The primary goal of this Web-mapping was to design and implement a web-based Geographic Information System (GIS) using open-source technology. This custom, comprehensive, and user-friendly geospatial system aimed to integrate and manage data from multiple end-users. The process of dissemination of cereal-growing information’s in sidi bel abbes, Algeria, over the Internet is presented as a successful implementation of this task, and can be easily deployed by a wide range of geographic information end users. [1]

articleTitle: A Uav-Based Close Monitoring of The Vegetation for Precision Agriculture Purposes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: This paper explores the application of "close" remote sensing technology for cost-effective and efficient monitoring of agricultural land. While traditional satellite monitoring has been transformative for large-scale observations,It faces limitations, especially when dealing with smaller-scale lands and capturing small target details. The solution lies in using drones equipped with multispectral cameras, offering precise and cost-efficient monitoring for smaller agricultural areas. The paper covers some general principles of optical remote sensing technology and techniques relevant to our application. We then assess the potential of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in agricultural applications, and subsequently, we developed an innovative aerial monitoring system for surveying vegetated areas. The integration of remote sensing and drone solutions emerges as a potential approach for revolutionizing cost-effective agricultural monitoring.

articleTitle: Landsat Time Series for Drought Monitoring: Application Using Google Earth Engine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: In recent years, this the Plain of Mekerra (Wilaya of Sidi Bel Abbes) region has been marked by signs of drought such as lack of rainfall and water stress in agricultural areas leading to shortage of agricultural crops. This requires scientific study in a systematic framework through the use of remote sensing indices to assess agricultural drought, including land surface temperature (LST), normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), temperature condition index (TCI) and vegetation condition index. (VCI) and vegetation health index (VHI). The integrated approach utilizing Google Earth Engine (GEE) cloud computing for automate crop drought analysis showcased notable correlation between the NDVI and key indicators. Specifically, NDVI-LST displayed a negative correlation of -0.73, NDVI-TCI showed a correlation of 0.73, while NDVI-VCI exhibited a strong correlation of 0.99, and NDVI-VHI demonstrated a correlation of 0.98. these significant correlations provide valuable insights into the relationships between NDVI and various agricultural indicators for drought monitoring and assessment.

articleTitle: Design and Building of Lora Based Communication Board for Educational Nanosatellite
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: This paper explores the integration of Long-Range (LoRa) communication technology into the Educational SATellite (ESAT) platform. Focused on advancing space education, the research introduces a LoRa-based communication board, enhancing the capabilities of the ESAT CubeSat kit. This addition empowers educational nanosatellites with long-range, low-power communication, aligning with the evolving CubeSat and IoT landscape. The ESAT kit's modular structure serves as a foundational tool for hands-on learning, making it an indispensable asset in the educational realm. The proposed LoRa technology augmentation opens new avenues for students to delve into remote sensing, collaborative data sharing, and environmental monitoring. Positioned at the forefront of educational space technology, this paper contributes to fostering innovation and expertise in nanosatellite design within educational institutions.

articleTitle: Assessing Urban Expansion of Algiers with Random Forest-Based Multi-Index Using Landsat Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: Urban sprawl is a global phenomenon characterized by the uncontrolled expansion of human settlements, negatively impacting the environment, economy, and society. Moreover, the evolution of urban sprawl had been identified as a significant factor contributing to various issues, including the intensification of the urban heat island effect in cities. In this study, we proposed an approach to analyze urban expansion based on the Random Forest Multi-Index classification (RaFMIC) using the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform. The Multi-Index approach integrates multiple indices derived from remote sensing data to enhance the accuracy and comprehensiveness of the classification process. For this purpose, multi-temporal Landsat data from 1995 to 2023 were used to generate classification maps of land use and land cover. The results obtained from the multi-index approach showed better classification performance when compared to SVM and CART methods. With an outstanding overall performance of 93.20% accuracy and a kappa value of 0.87 for all LULC classes, the methodology was applied to analyze urban expansion in Algiers (Algeria).

articleTitle: Wild Horse Optimization for Satellite Images Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: The use of satellite imagery has become an integral aspect in the planning of multiple domains that include disaster management and analysis of natural calamity images, snow cover mapping, smart city development, etc. Satellite images have now become an important area in remote sensing studies. The nature inspired optimization algorithms are very promising with image segmentation techniques to provide a platform for processing of satellite images. In this paper a new satellite image segmentation method is developed using Wild Horse Optimization (WHO) to cluster the image into disjoint regions based on color information. Experiments performed on two different satellite images confirm the stability, homogeneity, and the efficiency of proposed method with comparison to K-means and Shuffled Frog Leaping Algorithm (SFLA).

articleTitle: A Novel Residual-Concatenate Feature Fusion Strategy for Building Segmentation From Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel encoder-decoder architecture based on U-Net integrated with a residual-concatenate multi-scale feature fusion (RCMFF) strategy to perform efficient building segmentation from remote sensing images. The proposed method considers an end-to-end deep learning framework based on UNet that consists of mainly three modules: i) an encoder with convolutional block attention module (CBAM) employed in their lateral connections; ii) the proposed residual-concatenate multi-scale feature fusion (RCMFF) module; and finally, iii) a decoder with refinement layers. The proposed RCMFF module integrates semantically relevant discriminative features inherent within the last encoder layer with reduced number of parameters thereby simultaneously improving the segmentation accuracy as well as the computational speed. The effectiveness of the proposed module is assessed using two benchmark archives: Massachusetts (MAS) and WHU building datasets. The proposed model demonstrates an overall improvement of 2.30% and 7.01% compared to the baseline models DeepLabV3+ and UNet++, respectively.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach with Uncertainty Estimation to Assess Aboveground Biomass Mapping of Tropical Rainforest in Thailand
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Mediterranean and Middle-East Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (M2GARSS)
abstract: This study proposes an aboveground biomass (AGB) density model to overcome the limitation of sparse data coverage in Thailand and scale at national level. The model is based on a U-Net convolutional neural network and fuses spaceborne remote sensing data including Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and GEDI. Five models were developed using a deep ensemble technique to provide uncertainty estimation, where accuracy was validated using three types of forest inventory data. Tropical rainforests and other forested areas such as perennial crop regions with similar geographical characteristics were evaluated. Results show high uncertainty in the out-of-distribution data areas, with %RRMSE for Pará rubber, mixed deciduous forest, and dry evergreen forest of 17.05, 24.47, and 14.0, respectively.
